data.title: Highland Copper Reports Q1 2027 Financial and Operational Results
data.description:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Highland Copper Company Inc. (TSXV: HI; OTCQB: HDRSF) (“Highland” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce its financial and operational results for the three months ended September 30, 2026.

The Company’s unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements and accompanying Management’s Discussion and Analysis (“MD&A”) for the period ended September 30, 2026 are available under the Company’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the Company’s website at https://www.highlandcopper.com/investors/#financial-reports.

Q1 2027 Financial Highlights

  • Cash Position: Ended the quarter with $16.6 million in cash, compared to $18.9 million as of June 30, 2026.
  • Working Capital: Maintained positive working capital of $15.2 million as of September 30, 2026.
  • Net Loss: Recorded a net loss of $2.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 ($(0.00) per share) compared to net loss of $4.1 million during the comparative period last year ($(0.01) per share).

Selected Financial Results

The following table summarizes selected financial data for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025:

Q1 2027 Operational Highlights & Outlook

  • State Infrastructure Grant: The Company announced final approval by the Michigan Strategic Fund of $50 million in performance-based grant funding under the Strategic Site Readiness Program (“SSRP“) to support the development of the Company’s permitted Copperwood Project and related infrastructure improvements in Gogebic County, Michigan. The grant consists of:
    • US$45.0 million to Copperwood Resources Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Highland Copper, to support eligible infrastructure expenditures associated with the development of Copperwood; and
    • US$5.0 million to the Gogebic County Road Commission to support critical local infrastructure improvements associated with the Project and benefiting the broader region.
    • In addition to the SSRP funding, the Gogebic County Road Commission has secured a $7.5 million Transportation Economic Development Fund (“TEDF“) Category A grant from the Michigan Department of Transportation (“MDOT“).
    • Subsequent to quarter-end, Copperwood Resources Inc. concluded the formal grant agreement with the Michigan Strategic Fund. The grant is conditional upon the Company providing evidence, on or before March 31, 2028, that it has obtained commitments satisfactory to the MEDC for US$150,000,000 in additional project financing (the “Project Milestone”). Once the Company demonstrates that it has met the Project Milestone, it will be eligible for reimbursement of expenditures made on or before March 31, 2033, on site preparation and improvement necessary to support the development of the Project. The grant is subject to certain completion milestones, including that the Company has established a minimum of 380 qualified jobs at the Project.
  • Wetland Delineation and Permitting: As disclosed in the Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended June 30, 2026, the Company initiated a wetland delineation survey to inform whether a supplemental permit may be appropriate before construction. Given the passage of time since the original wetland delineation and permit, it was considered prudent to determine if new wetland had emerged that required permitting. Through this exercise, it was determined there is a modest amount of acreage that will require a supplemental Part 303 Wetland Protection permit. This is consistent with the assessment by Michigan's Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy. It is anticipated that the formal wetland delineation will conclude in Q2 2027 with a goal of receiving the permit by Q4 2027. 
  • Environmental Stewardship and Site Work: Continued early site work and environmental mitigation activities, including stream and wetland mitigation, revegetation, corrective work, and ongoing monitoring and maintenance. The Company also completed an off-site bridge replacement on budget and on time as a stream mitigation project and is in process to establish a 717-acre wetland preservation area.  
  • Integrated Mine Plan Review: Advanced the Integrated Mine Plan Review, including refinement of mine design criteria, mine design and production scheduling, geotechnical assumptions, infrastructure and equipment requirements, and operating cost estimates. The work is intended to optimize the Copperwood mine plan and establish an updated technical and cost basis for subsequent project engineering and the planned update to the Copperwood Feasibility Study.

Scientific and Technical Information

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Trace Arlaud, a “Qualified Person” as defined under NI 43-101. Ms. Arlaud is a consultant to Highland Copper and serves as the Company’s Project Director.

About Highland Copper Company

Highland Copper Company Inc. is a Canadian company focused on exploring and developing copper project in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan, U.S.A. The Company has 739,158,985 common shares issued and outstanding. Its common shares are listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol "HI" and trade on the OTCQB Venture Market under symbol "HDRSF".

More information about the Company is available on the Company’s website at www.highlandcopper.com and on SEDAR at www.sedar.com.

data.title: CARNIVAL CRUISE LINE UNVEILS THE NEXT WAVE OF VACATIONS FROM SEA TO SHORE, INCLUDING A NEW SHIP CLASS AND EXPANSION OF CELEBRATION KEY
data.description:
New Ships, Expanded Destinations and Enhanced Guest Experiences Shape Carnival's Next Chapter

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire-HISPANIC PR WIRE/ -- Carnival Cruise Line President Christine Duffy today announced plans for two new ships that will introduce a new class to the Carnival fleet. To be built by long-time partner Fincantieri and delivered in 2033 and 2035, the approximately 130,000-gross-ton LNG-powered ships are intentionally designed on a smaller scale, enabling access to more ports and expanding destination and itinerary choices.

"With a 29-ship fleet, we know our guests appreciate choices," said Duffy. "They love the incredible experiences and amenities on our Excel Class ships, the largest in our fleet, but they also love the intimacy our smaller ships offer. This new class gives us the best of both worlds, helping future-proof our fleet with the flexibility to take America's Cruise Line to even more places in the years ahead."

Duffy also shared a first look at Carnival Destiny, major expansions at Celebration Key, Grand Bahama, enhancements at RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay and plans to extend popular onboard benefits ashore. With more than 6.5 million guests sailing each year, Carnival has a unique perspective on what guests want from their vacations and is putting that feedback at the center of what comes next.

"Guests are seeking more choice, more flexibility and more ways to make the most of their time together," said Duffy. "What we are announcing today reflects how we're making Carnival cruise vacations even more personal, connected and fun."

Carnival Destiny Delivers More Choice with More Sea to See

Carnival Destiny, debuting in 2029 and the first of three Ace Class ships, is designed to give guests more ways to shape their cruise vacation around what they enjoy most. Built around its promise of More Sea to See, the ship will bring guests closer to the ocean with more outdoor space, expansive views and venues that make the sea part of the experience. Highlights include:

  • More outdoor pools than any other Carnival ship, including the first outward-facing main pool zone. Throughout the ship there will be eight pools, including six infinity pools, totaling more than 11,200 square feet of water surface,
  • An expansive ocean-front lanai that features several pools and brings dining and bar venues closer to the sea,
  • New premium venues with sweeping multideck ocean views, including a new exclusive pool on Deck 18 Aft, a total of 25 new dining and bar experiences, as well as a reimagined Limelight Lounge.

Carnival Destiny will dedicate nearly twice the space to family venues and attractions compared with Carnival's newest ships, bringing a family zone with mini golf, arcades, dining and other family favorites together in one area. It will also introduce Dr. Seuss Splash Station, a new splash pad inspired by The Cat in the Hat and Thing One and Thing Two, featuring water cannons and a dedicated area for children in swim diapers. The new attraction builds on Carnival's 13-year partnership with Dr. Seuss Enterprises and expands its popular Seuss at Sea programming.

Adults will have more choices of their own, with Carnival Destiny introducing Carnival's first adult-only zone spanning four decks. The zone will feature Carnival's first adult-only staterooms, an expanded Serenity adult-only retreat and an exclusive rooftop pool deck.

More Choice Ashore: The Next Evolution of Paradise Collection

Duffy also shared that Carnival is expanding the choices available ashore with the next evolution of Paradise Collection by Carnival, the largest portfolio of exclusive destinations across The Bahamas, Caribbean and Mexico.

The collection includes six distinct destinations: Celebration Key in Grand Bahama; RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay; Isla Tropicale in Roatan; Amber Cove in the Dominican Republic; Puerta Maya in Cozumel and Grand Turk in Turks & Caicos.

Building on the early success of Celebration Key, which has welcomed more than 3.25 million guests since its opening in July 2025, Carnival revealed plans for two new expansion phases for the destination that will increase total land-side capacity by 6,000 guests, with 3,000 added in each phase.

In 2028, a new portal will introduce even more ways for guests to play and relax together with a heated, beach-entry pool with a swim-up bar; a new social waterslide designed for four to five guests to slide together; and a colorful, aqua play area featuring five waterslides, a dry climbing play structure and drenching bucket created especially for younger children.

In 2030, a new major water park will add 18 waterslides, the cruise industry's longest lazy river with float-up bars and swim-in/swim-out cabanas, as well as a new exclusive area with an infinity pool, more beach access and new dining and bar concepts.

Carnival also announced Serenity Beach, a new complimentary retreat for guests 21 and older coming to RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay in spring 2027. It will feature dedicated loungers and bar and beverage service, with daybeds and cabanas available for an additional charge.

Greater Value from Ship to Shore

Beginning in February 2027, Carnival will extend its drink packages CHEERS!, CHEERS! Zero Proof™, Bottomless Bubbles™ and CHEERS! Social to Celebration Key and RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay, giving guests who purchase these Carnival packages greater value for their vacation dollars.

For additional information on Carnival Cruise Line and to book a cruise vacation on Carnival, call 1-800-CARNIVAL, visit http://carnival.com or contact your favorite travel advisor or online travel site.

ABOUT CARNIVAL CRUISE LINE

Carnival Cruise Line, part of Carnival Corporation (), the world's largest cruise company with a portfolio of cruise lines operating in over 800 ports & destinations worldwide – and is proud to be known as America's Cruise Line and for carrying more Americans and serving more U.S. homeports than any other. Carnival sails more than six and a half million guests annually and in 2023 was the first cruise line to sail more than 100 million guests in total. Operating from 13 U.S. and four Australian homeports, as well as seasonally from Europe, Carnival hosts more than 95,000 guests on its ships every day of the year and employs more than 50,000 team members, representing 120 nationalities.

Since its founding in 1972, Carnival has continually revolutionized the cruise industry and popularized the cruise vacation as an affordable and fun travel option. Carnival's fleet of 29 ships reflects an exciting period of growth that continues with the addition of seven ships through 2035: a fourth and fifth Excel class ship scheduled for 2027 and 2028, respectively; three Ace class ships scheduled for delivery in 2029, 2031 and 2033, beginning with Carnival Destiny; and two additional ships in the new class expected to be delivered in 2033 and 2035. Carnival's newest guest offering is its all-new exclusive destination, Celebration Key on Grand Bahama, which debuted in 2025 to join the company's Paradise Collection of Caribbean gems.

SOURCE Carnival Cruise Line

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow End Lower As Anthropic Trading Debut Fails To Provide Adequate Confidence —  ANT, META, AAPL, GME In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The S&P 500 eased about 2%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 2.2%, and the Dow Jones index fell 2.2% on Thursday. 
  • Market concerns regarding AI profitability, excessive spending, and heavy debt continue to weigh on sentiment.
  • Apple is reportedly working on its own AI agent. 

U.S. stock indices ended lower on Thursday, with the S&P 500 recording its longest losing streak since 2024 as Anthropic’s first trading session failed to lift investor sentiment.

The S&P 500 eased about 2%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 2.2%, and the Dow Jones index fell 2.2% on Thursday. The Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, ended 1.5% lower.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) fell 2% after-hours, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) eased 2.2%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) slipped 2.2%.

Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell close to 3.5% on Thursday, tracking broader index weakness. The broader Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT) fell about 2%.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bullish’ on the Invesco QQQ (QQQ), ‘bearish’ on the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA) and ‘neutral’ on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF, which track the benchmark indices at market close on Thursday.

US Market Drivers

IndexMoveClose
Dow Jones Industrial Average-2.2%49,097.06
S&P 500-2%7,175.83
Nasdaq 100-2.2%26,517.05

Anthropic closed its debut trading session 17% higher, but the market lost its footing mid-trading session on Thursday. Most benchmark technology indices and ETFs slipped to close lower.

The successful IPO did not seem to help investors overcome anxiety over bloated AI spending, incessant borrowing and overall profitability.

“The Anthropic IPO has been a major success,” Matt Maley at Miller Tabak told Bloomberg. “However, the IPO does little to address the market’s bigger problems including AI profitability concerns, massive spending, higher interest rates, credit market stress and geopolitical risks.”

However, Wharton professor Mohammed El-Erian noted that the dip in stock was about making room for Anthropic. “...remember this isn't just about the promise of AI, but about making room for it,” El-Erian wrote in a post on X.

Elsewhere, the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), often called Wall Street’s fear gauge, rose to its highest since March following Anthropic’s public debut as market participants pulled back from technology equities.

Krishna Rao, Anthropic’s chief financial officer (CFO), in an interview with Bloomberg, mentioned that the public market will give the company access to lower-cost financing that will help sustain the Claude developer’s aggressive research and development push.

Key Trending Stocks

Meta Platforms (META) plans to sell its upcoming Muse Charm for $300 and bundle promotional perks to jump-start demand for its compact artificial intelligence hardware.

‘The Big Short’ investor Michael Burry on Thursday disclosed several portfolio additions, beginning with Chinese electric-vehicle maker BYD, a direct Tesla competitor.

GameStop Inc. (GME) share price gained about 2% on Thursday after the U.S. Ethics Department disclosure for the month of November revealed a small buy-in by President Donald Trump in the video game retailer.

Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN) is preparing to launch internally operated prediction markets for U.S. customers in the first half of 2027, according to Bloomberg.

Apple Inc. (AAPL) is developing its own autonomous artificial intelligence agent, Bloomberg reported, sending Meta and Anthropic stocks lower in after-hours trading.

data.title: Anthropic listing extends Nasdaq's dominant run against arch-rival NYSE
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq IPOs raise about $201.8 billion this year versus $20.8 billion on NYSE, Dealogic data shows
  • Nasdaq finished ahead of NYSE six times in 2018 to 2025 period, according to Dealogic
  • New rules fast-track names like SpaceX into Nasdaq 100 index

By Anirban Sen

The market share battle between the two top US exchanges has never been so lopsided.

With Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering on Wednesday, Nasdaq snatched another marquee listing from the New York Stock Exchange this year, adding to its already wide lead in the battle for market share against its downtown rival. The exchange displayed the Anthropic win on the huge screens that envelop its Times Square address on Thursday, as more than 800 million shares changed hands in the AI company's debut.

"Anthropic’s IPO is a very proud moment for us," said Adena Friedman, chief executive officer of Nasdaq, in an interview Thursday. "We’ve been engaging with the Anthropic team for a very long time. Separate from the entire listing experience, we've been a client to them, as we are to the AI ecosystem, and so we also have gotten to know them in that context as well."

Over the last decade, the listing advantage has swung decisively in Nasdaq's favor. According to data from Dealogic, there have been 64 IPOs — led by Anthropic and SpaceX — on Nasdaq so far this year, raising about $201.8 billion, dwarfing the $20.8 billion haul raised from 42 IPOs on NYSE.

That is the widest gap in terms of capital raised between the two exchanges record since Dealogic started tracking the data in 1995. In 2017, NYSE raked in share sale proceeds of $28.8 billion from 69 deals, versus Nasdaq's $9.3 billion haul from 86 flotations. However, Nasdaq finished ahead of NYSE six out of eight times between 2018 and 2025, according to Dealogic, and is on track to do so again this year.

Nasdaq’s run of dominance can be linked to several moves the exchange operator has made over the years. Friedman, who has led Nasdaq for a decade, on Thursday cited the exchange operator's strength in marketing IPOs, its investor relations business that helps connect companies with large asset managers and institutional investors, and its index business — which it launched in 1985 — as key competitive advantages.

These efforts have allowed it to build relationships with founders in big IPO hubs like Silicon Valley and contributed to its dominance in tech listings.

"It's a very hard problem (for NYSE) to solve because Nasdaq didn't build its private markets business or its index just two years ago. They have had a head start of several years compared to their competitors. NYSE will have to probably just copy what Nasdaq has done for the past 10 years," said Owen Lau, an analyst at Clear Street.

NYSE executives are under increasing pressure to win the next mega-IPO after the recent losses to Nasdaq, according to two people familiar with the matter. The NYSE did not respond to a request for comment.

"Probably the major reason (for their dominance) is that Nasdaq has their own indexes," said Lau, referring to the Nasdaq 100 and the Nasdaq Composite , which are licensed for use by institutional asset managers. "That is a very big draw for many companies such as SpaceX and Anthropic."

The Nasdaq 100's constituents include several of the world's most valuable companies, such as Apple , Nvidia and Alphabet .

STRATEGIC ADVANTAGE

Admission to benchmarks like the Nasdaq 100 or S&P 500 gives companies increased access to deep-pocketed institutions with large index funds. This broadens the companies' shareholder base and improves share liquidity. The NYSE has a similar index that tracks its 100 largest US stocks that it launched last year, but it is less widely followed by investors.

Nasdaq introduced new rules earlier this year to speed the addition of newly listed megacap companies to the index, a move experts say gives them another advantage over the NYSE, even as it has drawn criticism from some quarters.

In an interview with Bloomberg in May, NYSE President Lynn Martin called the rule changes "questionable." On Thursday, Friedman said only a handful of megacap companies of the size and scale of Anthropic and SpaceX have the potential to be fast-tracked into the Nasdaq 100, adding that market liquidity is not an issue.

Reuters reported in March that SpaceX made early inclusion in the Nasdaq 100 a necessary condition to list on the Nasdaq. The exchange ultimately added the company to the index 15 days after its stock market debut.

data.title: Anthropic's $1.5 trillion debut rewrites venture capital's playbook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Spark led Anthropic's $450 million Series C in 2023 at a $4.5 billion valuation
  • Menlo invested over $1 billion for a stake of nearly 1.5%, a person familiar says
  • Amazon and Google together hold about 28.4% of Anthropic

By Krystal Hu

For decades, venture capital thrived on small bets that became billion-dollar companies.

Then came Anthropic , rewriting the playbook and forcing investors to write fatter checks to buy stakes at unheard-of valuations.

The AI lab’s shares began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday at a $1.5 trillion valuation, delivering multibillion-dollar windfalls to venture investors at a moment when the industry needs fresh liquidity to fund more bets on AI companies. The stock closed at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price of $83.

Anthropic's stock market value ended the day at about $1.3 trillion, based on its outstanding shares, or $1.8 trillion, based on its fully diluted shares.

To join the fundraising frenzy, especially at later stages, venture capital firms invested billions, tapping their own investors for additional capital through special-purpose vehicles.

MENLO, SPARK REAP BIG RETURNS

Menlo Ventures and Spark Capital emerged with some of the biggest returns by multiple. Spark Capital was the first venture capital firm to lead an Anthropic investment, in a $450 million Series C round in 2023 at a valuation of $4.5 billion. Spark general partner Yasmin Razavi, who spearheaded the investment, remains the only investor who sits on Anthropic’s board.

Writing the largest check in the firm’s history, early-stage firm Menlo invested over $1 billion for a stake of nearly 1.5%, according to a person familiar with the investment. At a $1.5 trillion market cap, Menlo’s stake is worth over $20 billion.

To invest beyond the capacity of its existing fund, Menlo raised a $750 million special-purpose vehicle from limited partners, a tactic that became increasingly common as funding rounds grew, given the capital needs of AI companies.

THE LATE-STAGE BETS PAID OFF

Sequoia Capital, long known for its early bets, joined a later round and still stands to earn billions of dollars.

Sequoia passed on Anthropic at lower prices. After a leadership change, it wrote its first check at the start of this year, joining a round led by Singapore’s GIC and Coatue at a $380 billion post-money valuation in February. It later co-led, alongside Altimeter, Dragoneer and Greenoaks, a round at $965 billion. Sequoia has invested $3 billion in Anthropic and continued to invest more through Anthropic's IPO, signaling further conviction in the AI lab.

Lightspeed Venture Partners, which invested more than $3 billion in Anthropic, now holds over 2% of the company, making it the largest financial investor in the company, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The returns are possible because of the rapid rise in Anthropic’s valuation and revenue. Its annualized revenue grew from about $1 billion at the start of 2025 to about $81 billion last month, as its valuation climbed from $61.5 billion in March 2025 to $965 billion in the latest private round this May.

Strategic backers, too, supply much of the unprecedented capital and computing power needed by AI labs. The combined stake of Amazon and Alphabet's Google in Anthropic is about 28.4%.

“We're living through a very unique time of profound change happening at a higher velocity than ever before. The scale of the impact of these businesses and the breadth of market opportunities is larger than anything we've seen before. And that is going to afford investment opportunities that are larger than what we've seen in the past,” said Will Griffith, a partner at Iconiq, which has invested $6.1 billion, making the fund the second-largest financial investor by ownership in Anthropic.

data.title: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern Look Forward to a Full Evaluation of Merger Application
data.description:
Union Pacific () and Norfolk Southern () today filed their response to Canadian Pacific Kansas City’s request that the Surface Transportation Board (STB) terminate review of the proposed transcontinental railroad, which will be the nation’s first single-line, seamless coast-to-coast railroad.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119356896/en/

As made clear in their response and an accompanying verified statement from CEO Jim Vena, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern consistently support a full, transparent and rigorous review of the proposed merger and encourage all stakeholders to make their views known to the STB.

“I have spoken publicly in front of numerous groups before and since the merger announcement. I have also spoken to and with hundreds of our customers. I do use humor in my presentations to keep the audience engaged, including in my presentation at the conference of the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers this past March. I know what I said and regret the inference. The speech was over 50 minutes long, and I made an attempt at humor at the end of that presentation. I apologize to anyone who misunderstood my statement,” said Vena.

data.title: Ross Stores sees holiday sales growth slowing on lower discretionary spending; shares down
data.description:
By Neil J Kanatt and Shania S Thomas

Ross Stores maintained its holiday-quarter sales growth forecast on Thursday despite a strong third quarter, signaling a slowdown from the off-price retailer's traffic-driven gains in recent months, sending shares down about 5% in extended trading.

The company expects comparable store sales to rise 4% to 5% in the fourth quarter, compared with an 8% increase in the third quarter and a 9% gain in the year-ago holiday period.

Here are some details:

  • The off-price retailer faces pressure from weaker discretionary spending from consumers and intense competition from value-focused offerings from discount chains and fast-fashion retailers

  • "There's a lot of inflationary pressure. Consumer confidence is extremely low," CEO James Conroy said in a post-earnings call

  • The company also lowered its quarterly earnings forecast by 1 cent at both ends of its range to $2.16 to $2.25 per share but raised its annual earnings per share forecast to $8.75 to $8.84 from $8.61 to $8.77 previously, aided by year-to-date strength

  • "People knew Ross results would be great, which, fair or not, prompts investors to ask whether it was 'great enough'," Guggenheim Securities analyst Simeon Siegel said

  • Ross posted third-quarter earnings per share of $1.91, versus estimates of $1.88; revenue rose 12% to $6.3 billion, in line with expectations

  • "The company's investments in merchandising, marketing, and the shopping experience appear to be paying off ... However, investors want to see that momentum translate into stronger earnings," eMarketer analyst Arielle Feger said

data.title: Record profits but record outflows: 'Sell Korea' trade stalks Seoul market
data.description:
Key points:
  • KOSPI down 44% from June's record high, remains up 20% year-to-date
  • Record profits at Samsung and SK Hynix no panacea as buybacks dry up
  • Equity outflows stretch to seventh month, drawdown eclipses any since 2008

By Gregor Stuart Hunter and Heekyong Yang

South Korea's biggest companies are posting record AI-driven profits and the stock market is among the world's cheapest, yet foreign investors keep heading for the exits — and with buybacks winding down, few buyers are left to step in.

No major equity index rode the AI boom harder than Seoul's KOSPI , which hit a record in June but has since lost 44%, wiping out some 3.3 quadrillion won ($2.4 trillion) in market value as doubts grow over the debt-fuelled AI infrastructure buildout.

That's even as earnings vaulted ninefold and sevenfold, respectively, to unprecedented levels at Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix , the dominant makers globally of the AI memory chips needed by data centres. Together, the companies make up nearly half the KOSPI's value.

It demonstrates a disconnect in the market, which analysts say is now driven less by corporate fundamentals than by a lack of buyers, and points to a swift loss of conviction among investors for the chipmakers at the heart of the AI trade.

"We're essentially experiencing a full-fledged 'Sell Korea' trend," said Han Jiyoung, an analyst at Kiwoom Securities in Seoul.

"The challenge for the market now is to find a catalyst that could bring foreign investors back."

Foreigners are on course to sell Korean stocks for a seventh straight month in November, with cumulative net outflows of $115.2 billion marking the biggest retreat on record in LSEG data to the start of 2008.

Overseas purchases of leveraged single-stock ETFs, particularly ones tied to SK Hynix in Hong Kong , fuelled outsized gains on the way up, but ultimately accelerated the speed and depth of the rout.

Corporate share buybacks, which had soaked up much of the foreign selling in recent months, are also easing off. Retail investors, who are still nursing losses from a wrenching selloff that started in June, may struggle to fill the gap.

FUNDAMENTALS VS FLOWS

Record profits at South Korea's two biggest firms have resulted in eye-popping shareholder-return plans for 2026, worth as much as 210 trillion won combined, including buybacks, dividends and share cancellations. But with the end of those programs approaching, markets are on edge.

Responding to Reuters questions on Thursday, Samsung Electronics reiterated plans to return up to 110 trillion won to shareholders for 2026, saying its board would finalise the scale and execution of the remaining returns in late January.

SK Hynix also reaffirmed plans to return about 100 trillion won to shareholders through share buybacks and cancellations, adding that it would continue quarterly share repurchases and pay special dividends on significant investment gains.

The sentiment around the AI trade has worsened markedly in recent weeks, after the emphatic victory by Democrats in this month's US midterms fuelled worries about a slowdown in data-centre construction. Washington's restrictions on advanced chip supply to several US trading partners in Asia and Latin America have exacerbated worries further.

"There's a capitulation, where positions are shifting away from anything linked to AI into anything defensive, high quality and stable," said Isaac Thong, a portfolio manager at the Aberdeen Asian Income Fund in Singapore.

"Why it doesn't feel like previous down cycles is because fundamentally things are still really strong in the AI world," he said. "There's a lot of confidence at a corporate level, at least in the shorter term."

Last month, Samsung said chip supplies were expected to remain tight through 2028, while SK Hynix painted a similarly bullish picture of demand, pointing to an even longer supply crunch.

Goldman Sachs lowered its target on the KOSPI this week for the second time since the end of October, to 7,500 from 12,000, "to account for the market’s continued reluctance to fully price in fundamentals."

"We still see Korea offering the greatest potential upside among regional markets," Goldman strategists said. The KOSPI closed at 5,062.92 on Wednesday, still up 20% this year in local currency terms.

Korean stocks trade at a substantial discount to global peers, with MSCI's country gauge trading at a multiple of 3.27 times forward earnings, compared to 15.35 times for the MSCI All-Country World index, according to LSEG Datastream.

Tighter regulation and other guardrails after the US midterms could eventually raise costs and slow the AI buildout, according to Seoul-based Sanjeev Rana, head of North Asia semiconductor research at CLSA.

But given how important AI infrastructure is to the US economy and jobs, Rana expects most of the capacity needed to support AI's growth to be built, even if the pace slows or other countries take up the slack.

In the medium term, "the elections and the changing political landscape doesn't change the outlook in any meaningful way," he said.

"Earnings for 2027 are still pretty much in the bag."

data.title: Germany launches dialogue on economic future
data.description:
Germany's finance ministry is launching a dialogue process to develop proposals for the future of Europe's largest economy, ministry officials said on Friday.

Here are more details:

  • The guiding questions are how to secure growth and prosperity and what role forward-looking fiscal policy can play.

  • Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil will open the process on December 2 at an event where he will welcome economists from around the world.

  • A call for workshop proposals starts on Friday. Think tanks, research organisations, universities and civil society groups are asked to host workshops in the first half of 2027.

  • The ministry is working on 12 topics, including tax and fiscal policy, investment and domestic demand, industrial policy, energy and climate transition, foreign trade and sovereignty, and housing and local infrastructure.

  • A two-day conference in Berlin next year is meant to link the expert debate with a wider public discussion.

  • The process is to end in a white paper with recommendations for Germany's economic future up to 2035. Publication is planned for 2028.

data.title: German tax revenue down 2.6% in October
data.description:
By Maria Martinez

Germany's federal and state government tax revenue fell by 2.6% in October compared with the same month a year ago, the finance ministry said in its monthly report on Friday.

  • Total tax revenue reached €59.6 billion ($65.35 billion)

  • Income tax and corporation tax fell substantially in October

  • Revenue from federal taxes fell by 4% in October compared with the same month a year earlier, mainly due to lower revenue from energy tax on fuels

  • Tax revenue for the January-to-October period rose by 0.6% year-on-year to €730.2 billion

  • Tax experts see tax revenue increasing to €911.0 billion in 2026, up 1.0% year-on-year

($1 = 0.9121 euros)

data.title: Cyber and drone incidents point to a more unstable world
data.description:
Key points:
  • US-China-Russia talks highlight uncertain global backdrop
  • Microsoft and US air traffic control outages stir unease
  • Smaller countries seek to navigate risks by collaborating

By Peter Apps

As multiple computer systems crashed around the world last week and unidentified drones piled pressure on US air bases in Britain, Southeast Asian nations firmed up plans to build and share oil supplies in the event of a major crisis.

Their move was overshadowed by the run-up to Thursday's talks between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia — Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin — in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

It was a meeting that gave the White House a chance to demonstrate its power and reach despite the loss of both houses of Congress to the Democrats.

But as the Asian energy security effort shows, for countries watching from the sidelines, the focus is increasingly on a host of fast-growing risks that they may need to manage with much less leadership from Washington.

COMPETITION, VOLATILITY AND FRAGMENTATION CAUSE CONCERN

Even after Trump returned to the White House at the start of 2025, plenty of traditional US allies maintained their trust in Washington and international structures to manage increasingly assertive and sometimes aggressive Moscow and Beijing.

This year has, however, delivered such a range of shocks – some direct from the White House, others from new dynamics including the rise of AI – that a range of governments are gradually but radically adjusting their world view.

"The world has changed," Australian Secretary to the Treasury Jenny Wilkinson told the Economic Security Forum in Sydney this month, pointing to "intensifying geopolitical competition and a more volatile and fragmented international environment".

Another speaker, Marco Buti, a professor and former director general for economic and financial affairs at the European Commission, used the phrase "predatory superpowers" to refer to Washington, Moscow and Beijing.

While all three capitals reject the characterisation, its airing at such an event underlines a growing nervousness elsewhere that the United States, Russia and China are delivering disruption that other powers must learn to manage.

Broader drivers of rising instability include the growing strength of technology, particularly drones and rapidly developed AI "frontier models", as well as uncertainty over long-term access to other vital infrastructure and resources.

Those dynamics are not new – but the combination of technological and political unpredictability now frequently outstrips anything seen in recent history.

This week, OpenAI executive Dean Ball described in an essay what he called a growing "silent consensus" in Silicon Valley that increased algorithmic decision-making was now on the brink of taking over.

"Taken together, the decisions could produce a world in which people have forfeited effective authority over much of our civilisation," he wrote, adding that this was a vision he "despised" but was becoming increasingly privately widespread among the tech elite.

On one level, traditional US allies like to think they have a plan, at least to deal with growing conflict risks: deepening coordination with the Pentagon.

But while in NATO, Asia and the Middle East there is growing coordination with the US Project Maven AI-enabled command and control system, officials have expressed concern that in a crisis they might be denied access to US AI or satellites.

MAJOR SYSTEMS FAILURES LEAVE UNANSWERED QUESTIONS

Coupled with that is nervousness that the US may no longer have a handle on key events. Last week's disruption to US air traffic control and key Microsoft systems as well as details of the use in China of cutting-edge AI chips from tech firm Nvidia have only fuelled those fears.

On their own, these incidents or trends might well have been largely ignored by economic, military or investment planners and officials keen to focus on the bigger picture.

Increasingly, however, that is no longer possible: governments are now being forced to face up to fragmentation, although for now they are taking very mixed levels of action.

Gauging the true range and nature of potential danger, though, is often far from easy – even after significant disruption has begun. Questions remain over the exact causes of last week's 24-hour blackout of key Microsoft services including email program Outlook on which many companies and governments depend, as well as the failure shortly after of US air traffic control systems.

According to briefings from Microsoft and US government officials, neither incident was down to a conventional or AI-enabled cyberattack, or other external action, but instead to cascading glitches and then wider failures heavily driven by legacy code and equipment issues.

US officials similarly denied a cyberattack was responsible for a "degradation" of services at the US National Security Agency or that the three major incidents in a single week meant the US was under concerted attack.

"We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Manila on Wednesday.

The unidentified drone activity at a US air base in Britain last week came after bombers used to strike Iran were moved out of Britain following the arrest of five men near another base.

Other nations to report unauthorised and unidentified drone activity near major bases include Australia in August.

The nature of both cyber intrusions and targeting of sensitive facilities by drones, of course, can quite deliberately make attribution difficult. Both offer cheap routes to threaten, damage or at least temporarily disrupt essential infrastructure, sometimes while avoiding blame.

On Tuesday, Norway's oil and gas company Equinor reported that it was under an ongoing cyberattack, declining to give more details.

DISRUPTION AND DESTRUCTION FORCE GOVERNMENTS TO RETHINK

Some of the most recent disruption is likely to be explained in part by technical breakthroughs: AI programs now finding so many vulnerabilities and then alerting operators to them in ways that overwhelm tech firms and governments alike.

On Tuesday, Google's Threat Intelligence Group warned that a new era of "autonomous attacks" in cyberspace had now arrived, with hackers able to delegate much of their work to AI agents that probe relentlessly for vulnerabilities without human input.

Drones are also now in much more plentiful supply, with skills and technologies built amid fighting in Ukraine increasingly for sale to those with the ability to pay.

Drone attacks have killed many people in Sudan, where the military is fighting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, but international willingness to tackle such conflicts is now at its lowest for several decades, as also seen repeatedly in Gaza.

In some cases, collaboration and innovative use of new technology can still deliver considerable effect. In the Baltic Sea, officials credit NATO's Operation Baltic Sentry — pulling together drones and pre-existing regional intelligence feeds — for a significant reduction in disruption to undersea cables, which officials attribute to fast identification of culprits.

Considerable risks remain, however, particularly if hostile nations choose to rip up international rules. One recent private wargame in Singapore suggested a couple of cargo ships carrying autonomous attack drones would be enough to bring that territory to its knees, perhaps as part of a potential larger conflict.

Risk tolerance may be increasing. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said this month that Warsaw had been warned armed groups may try to enter Poland over its eastern borders and that guards had prevented a "provocation".

Chinese naval activity around Taiwan has been high as Xi, Putin and Trump approached their meeting, with Beijing also extending its ban on rare-earth exports last week until the end of January.

So-called "middle powers" have clearly found the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting optics unsettling. They may find they have to do much more to regain their agency in a world now shifting in strange and complex ways.

data.title: Intuit's downbeat outlook deepens Wall Street's anxiety about software companies
data.description:
By Claudia Assis

Software and fintech company to sell Mailchimp business to Bending Spoons

Intuit cut its outlook for fiscal 2027, renewing worries about legacy software companies.

TurboTax maker Intuit is giving investors a fresh reason to worry about legacy software companies.

Intuit's stock (INTU) dropped more than 10% in the after-hours session Thursday after the fintech and software company cut its outlook for fiscal 2027.

That played into concerns that Intuit and other traditional software companies may be ill-equipped to fend off AI disruption and increased competition from AI tools.

Broad worries about software security that surfaced after several recent, well-publicized crashes have played a part. Heading into earnings, Intuit's stock had lost more than 9% on the week, and it was off 53% year to date.

The company also announced a deal to sell its Mailchimp marketing and e-mail business to Italian tech conglomerate Bending Spoons (BSP) for $3.7 billion in cash and stock.

Intuit called for revenue of between $23.1 billion and $23.4 billion for the fiscal year that ends next July. That compares with the FactSet consensus for $23.4 billion. The company in September had modeled revenue of between $23.3 billion and $23.5 billion for the 2027 fiscal year.

The changes centered on Credit Karma, Intuit's consumer credit-monitoring platform, the company said.

Intuit dialed back expectations for Credit Karma's fiscal 2027 revenue to between $2.72 billion and $2.83 billion, from a previous expectation of $2.92 billion to $2.97 billion.

The deal with Bending Spoons for Mailchimp is expected to close early next year, and the outlook will be updated then, Intuit said.

Intuit reported adjusted earnings of $2.91 a share, compared with the FactSet consensus for adjusted earnings of $2.46 a share. Intuit is focused on "disciplined execution as we build durable, long-term growth," CEO Sasan Goodarzi said in a statement.

-Claudia Assis

data.title: Corpay Invests Alongside TPG to Acquire BILL
data.description:
Corpay, Inc. (), the global spend management company, today announced that it has signed a definitive agreement to make a $1.1 billion minority investment in BILL () as part of a transaction to take BILL private alongside TPG for $63.25 per share that values BILL at $6.0 billion.

Under the agreement, Corpay will invest $1.1 billion for an approximately one-third equity stake in the company with the option to acquire 100% of the company. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval and standard closing conditions.

BILL is an intelligent finance platform and leading provider of spend management and accounts payable solutions to small and lower middle market businesses, with an especially unique distribution network of accountants.

“We’re delighted to partner with BILL leadership and TPG on this transaction. Given our successful relationship with TPG, we are excited to participate in this transaction and invest in another large, complementary corporate payments business,” said Ron Clarke, Chairman and CEO of Corpay.

“We expect the transaction to be accretive to Corpay cash EPS in 2027, and the take-private transaction structure gives the company the flexibility to transform and accelerate profit growth. We have the option to buy the rest of the company in 2030,” said Peter Walker, CFO of Corpay.

“Corpay has a long track record of driving value through innovative products and high-quality customer service,” said John Flynn and Tim Millikin, Partners at TPG. “This joint investment is grounded in a shared conviction in the long-term growth opportunities across financial technology and payments where our respective expertise and capabilities will further support BILL’s next chapter of growth.”

Barclays acted as exclusive financial advisor to Corpay, and Sullivan & Cromwell LLP acted as legal counsel to Corpay.
